[Line 01]{.eyebrow}

## Urban scaling and metabolism

Cities are not scaled-up or scaled-down versions of one another: their properties
change systematically and non-linearly with population size. We study how
productivity, occupational diversity, water consumption and material footprint scale
across Chilean cities, and what that implies for planning.

[Line 02]{.eyebrow}

## Interaction networks and segregation

Segregation is not only residential. Using voice-call networks across cities in Chile
and Brazil, we measure *interactional* segregation: who people actually communicate
with along the socioeconomic gradient, and how that structure departs from what
surveys report.

[Line 03]{.eyebrow}

## Computational ecology and conservation

Species distribution modelling, landscape fragmentation analysis, and assessment of
wildfire and irrecoverable carbon loss in Chile's protected areas, centred on the
Valdivian temperate rainforest.
